summary: Riding a minecart cluster into a wall freezes the game
description: Derailed Minecarts that are clustered together often keep their movement speed, which is due to another bug (). In some cases (with the Minecart Improvements experiment enabled) if such clusters of minecarts are ridden by the player and collide with blocks, the screen goes black and the game stops working. It then has to be terminated manually. Steps to reproduce (or use the link below for a more reliable method): - Place around 20 to 30 minecarts on a normal rail. - Push the minecarts. They should now start to move off the rail, keeping their velocity. - Ride one of the minecarts in the cluster. - Wait until it collides into blocks (2 blocks high is best). Water like in the attached videos isn t needed. This is not very reliable, so a few attempts may be needed. Alternatively, the attached world ( ) can be used to reproduce the bug: - Open the world. - Walk into the minecart cluster. - Ride one of the minecarts in the cluster. - Wait until it collides into the wall and locks the game.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
3. Place around 20 to 30 minecarts on a normal rail.
4. Push the minecarts to start their movement off the rail, ensuring they keep their velocity.
5. Ride one of the minecarts in the cluster.
6. Wait until the minecart collides with a wall (2 blocks high is best).
7. Observe that the screen goes black and the game stops working, requiring manual termination.
Observed Behavior: When a player rides a cluster of derailed minecarts that maintain their speed and collides with a wall, the game experiences a freeze, resulting in a black screen and necessitating a manual termination of the application. This issue occurs specifically when the Minecart Improvements experiment is enabled. To reproduce the bug, players should place approximately 20 to 30 minecarts on standard rails and push them to initiate movement off the rail while retaining their velocity. The player then rides one of the moving minecarts in the cluster until it collides with solid blocks, preferably two blocks high, although water is not required for this process. It may take several attempts to consistently trigger the freeze, as the occurrence is not entirely reliable. An alternative method involves using an attached world file where players can simply walk into the minecart cluster, ride one of the minecarts, and wait for it to collide with a wall, which will cause the game to lock up.
Expected Behavior: When riding a minecart cluster that is moving at full speed, the player should be able to collide with blocks without causing the game to freeze or the screen to go black. Instead, upon impact, the minecarts should come to a safe and controlled stop, allowing the player to dismount normally and continue gameplay without any interruptions or crashes. This behavior should be consistent across all versions, including those with the Minecart Improvements experiment enabled.
